title: Structural Fine-Tuning under Economic Restrictions
abstract: arXiv:2611.25420v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How should a predictor trained on historical data be adapted to a new economic environment or task when few target observations are available? We propose structural fine-tuning, a framework that introduces economic restrictions to guide the adaptation of pretrained predictors. The framework does not require a complete structural model; instead, it utilizes constraints based on economic knowledge, ranging from simple, ubiquitous assumptions to particular workhorse models. Theoretically, we characterize conditions when economic restrictions improve prediction over the original model and ordinary fine-tuning. Then, we illustrate the framework through a simulation exercise of a credit issuer's credit-limit decision following a Medicaid-style expansion in medical payments. translated_title: 经济约束下的结构化微调
translated_abstract: 当仅有少量目标观测数据可用时，基于历史数据训练的预测器应如何适配到新的经济环境或任务中？我们提出了“结构化微调”这一框架，通过引入经济约束来指导预训练预测器的适配。该框架不需要完整的结构模型；相反，它利用基于经济知识的约束，这些约束的范围涵盖从简单、普遍的假设到特定的经典模型。在理论层面，我们刻画了经济约束在何种条件下能够比原始模型和普通微调改进预测。随后，我们通过一个模拟实验来说明该框架：模拟医疗支付实施“医疗补助（Medicaid）式”扩张后，信贷机构的信贷额度决策。通过施加基于资格认定、未偿医疗账单、现金流和群体层面风险界限的约束，我们的框架降低了预测的均方根误差。
tldr: 提出了“结构化微调”框架，在不要求完整结构模型的前提下，利用经济约束指导预训练预测器在少样本新经济环境中的适配，从理论上刻画了经济约束改进预测的条件，并通过信贷额度决策模拟验证了其降低预测误差的效果。
en_tdlr: Proposes "structural fine-tuning," a framework that uses economic restrictions—without requiring a full structural model—to guide the adaptation of pretrained predictors to new economic environments with few observations, theoretically characterizes when such restrictions improve prediction over ordinary fine-tuning, and demonstrates reduced prediction error in a credit-limit decision simulation.
